decisions.reason: The reference class electrometer belongs to the firm's core dosimetry business, has been featured on the home page for two years, and costs little to keep while it builds value.

The oncology risk management software is further from the firm's hardware core and its value is still uncertain, but it has kept its own page for two years and maintaining it costs little, so keeping the option open is justified.
The CT phantom was launched only in 2024 and fits the firm's QA portfolio, so its uncertainty has not yet resolved and keeping it is cheap.
The mammography phantom is a new, low-cost catalogue item whose value cannot yet be judged, so the option stays open.
The full field mammography phantom overlaps somewhat with Product D, but it is too early for results to justify dropping it and keeping it costs little.
This broad line of imaging QA instruments extends the core business into a growing area, and there is no evidence yet against it.
